speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when your gait and limb ataxia first began, and if you've noticed any other symptoms like vision changes or memory loss?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any recent head trauma, and do you have a history of alcohol use or neurological conditions? Also, are you currently taking any new medications or experiencing any numbness or tingling?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your Crohn's disease and treatment with natalizumab, I am concerned about a potential infection, so have you had any recent fevers, headaches, or neck stiffness? I would also like to know if you have noticed any changes in your vision or new weakness in your limbs.

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had a recent fever or major infection that I know of. The symptoms are mostly gait imbalance, limb ataxia, and weaker use of my right arm.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of natalizumab use and new neurological deficits, I need to rule out a specific opportunistic infection. REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast. REQUEST TEST: CSF analysis for JC virus PCR.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Vital signs are normal (Normothermic, BP/HR/RR within normal range). Neurological examination reveals ataxic gait, limb ataxia, and right upper limb weakness (4/5 strength). MRI Brain findings show multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). CSF analysis results for JC virus PCR are not available in the provided data.

speaker: Doctor
text: The MRI findings of multifocal demyelinating lesions in a patient on natalizumab are highly suggestive of Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML), though the pending CSF result is critical for confirmation. Since the JC virus PCR is not yet available, I will proceed with the clinical diagnosis based on the strong imaging evidence and medication history. DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML)
